Graph input shape: {persons: [{id, gender, dob, birth_order}], couples: [{couple_id, partner_a, partner_b}], child_of: [{couple_id, child_person_id}]}. Derive edges: parents(P) = the two partners of any couple C where P appears in child_of(C); children(P) = children of couples where P is a partner; spouse(P) = the other partner of a couple containing P; fullSiblings(P) = other children of the same parent-couple.
Algorithm: BFS over undirected edges (up=to parent, down=to child, sp=to spouse) from fromId to toId, shortest path wins, deterministic tie-break order up < sp < down. Convert the edge sequence to a canonical relation key per the REQUIRED KEYS list. Spouses of relatives append an sp hop (e.g. up,up,sp for father's elder brother's wife). Cousins: parent's sibling's child collapses to key "cousin". Grandparents distinguished paternal/maternal by which parent the up-up path goes through. Nephew/niece precision kept as brother_son / brother_daughter / sister_son / sister_daughter. Unknown shapes (e.g. spouse's sibling, cycles, disconnected) return relation_key null with the path found.
Relation keys (REQUIRED, canonical): self, spouse, fa, mo, son, daughter, brother_el, brother_yo, sister_el, sister_yo, grandfa_pat, grandmo_pat, grandfa_mat, grandmo_mat, grandson, granddaughter, fa_br_el, fa_br_yo, fa_si, mo_br, mo_si_el, mo_si_yo, fa_br_el_sp, fa_br_yo_sp, fa_si_sp, mo_br_sp, mo_si_sp, brother_son, brother_daughter, sister_son, sister_daughter, cousin.
